sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: Recognitions for outstanding achievements in various fields like **science, literature, arts, sports, social service, bravery**, and **public service**.

Many significant awards were established in the **late 19th and 20th centuries**. For example, the **Nobel Prize** in **1901**, **Bharat Ratna** in **1954**, **Padma Awards** in **1954**, **Arjuna Award** in **1961**, **Booker Prize** in **1969**, **Pulitzer Prize** in **1917**.

Locations vary: **Stockholm, Sweden** (most Nobel Prizes), **Oslo, Norway** (Nobel Peace Prize), **Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi** (Indian National Awards), **various international venues** for global awards.

Individuals, groups, or organizations demonstrating **exceptional talent, dedication, and impact** in their respective domains. Includes **scientists, writers, artists, athletes, social workers, and political leaders**.
They **motivate excellence**, **recognize contributions**, **inspire future generations**, and **highlight significant achievements** that benefit society. They also preserve history and culture.
Often include a **medal, citation, and a cash prize**. Some are awarded **posthumously**. Categories can be **national, international, civilian, military, sports, or literary**.

A crucial General Awareness topic. Questions frequently cover **first recipients, recent winners, award categories, associated fields, and key facts** about major Indian and International awards. Focus on **dates, names, and specific achievements**.

Includes **Nobel Prize, Bharat Ratna, Padma Awards (Vibhushan, Bhushan, Shri), Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award, Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, Booker Prize, Pulitzer Prize, Oscar, Grammy, Ramon Magsaysay Award**, and **Olympic medals**.

items.title: 1. The **Nobel Prize**: Global Pinnacle of Achievement
items.content:
• Established by **Alfred Nobel**, Swedish inventor of dynamite.
• First awarded in **1901**.
• Categories: **Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace**, and **Economic Sciences** (added in **1968** by Sweden's central bank).
• Presented annually on **December 10** (Nobel's death anniversary).
• Peace Prize awarded in **Oslo, Norway**; others in **Stockholm, Sweden**.
• Key Indian Laureates:
  • **Rabindranath Tagore** (Literature, **1913** - first non-European)
  • **C.V. Raman** (Physics, **1930**)
  • **Mother Teresa** (Peace, **1979**)
  • **Amartya Sen** (Economic Sciences, **1998**)
  • **Kailash Satyarthi** (Peace, **2014**)
• **Mnemonic for Nobel Categories:** **P**eace **L**oves **M**y **E**conomic **P**hysics & **C**hemistry. (Peace, Literature, Medicine, Economic Sciences, Physics, Chemistry)

items.title: 2. Indian Civilian Honours: **Bharat Ratna** & **Padma Awards**
items.content:
• **Bharat Ratna**:
  • India's **highest civilian award**.
  • Instituted in **1954**.
  • Awarded for **exceptional service/performance of the highest order** in any field of human endeavour.
  • Maximum **three** awards in a year.
  • Can be awarded **posthumously** (provision added in **1966**).
  • First recipients (**1954**): **C. Rajagopalachari, Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman**.
  • Recent notable recipients: **Pranab Mukherjee, Bhupen Hazarika, Nanaji Deshmukh** (**2019**).
• **Padma Awards**:
  • Instituted in **1954**.
  • Three categories, in decreasing order of importance:
    1.  **Padma Vibhushan**: For **exceptional and distinguished service**.
    2.  **Padma Bhushan**: For **distinguished service of a high order**.
    3.  **Padma Shri**: For **distinguished service**.
  • Announced annually on **Republic Day**.
  • **Mnemonic for Padma Awards Hierarchy:** **V**ery **B**ig **S**ervice (Vibhushan, Bhushan, Shri).

items.title: 3. Indian Sports Awards: **Arjuna**, **Dronacharya**, **Khel Ratna**
items.content:
• **Arjuna Award**:
  • Instituted in **1961**.
  • Recognizes **outstanding performance in sports and games** over the previous **four years**.
  • Named after **Arjuna**, a character from the Mahabharata.
  • Includes a bronze statue of Arjuna, a certificate, and a cash prize of **₹15 lakh**.
• **Dronacharya Award**:
  • Instituted in **1985**.
  • Recognizes **outstanding coaches** in sports and games.
  • Named after **Dronacharya**, the royal guru to the Pandavas and Kauravas.
  • Includes a bronze statue of Dronacharya, a certificate, and a cash prize of **₹15 lakh**.
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** (formerly Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award):
  • India's **highest sporting honour**.
  • Instituted in **1991-92**.
  • Awarded for **spectacular and most outstanding performance** in sports over the previous **four years**.
  • First recipient: **Viswanathan Anand** (Chess).
  • Includes a medal, a certificate, and a cash prize of **₹25 lakh**.

items.title: 4. International Literary Awards: **Booker Prize** & **Pulitzer Prize**
items.content:
• **Booker Prize** (formerly Man Booker Prize):
  • Established in **1969**.
  • Awarded annually for the **best original novel written in English** and published in the **UK or Ireland**.
  • Key Indian/Indian-origin winners: **V.S. Naipaul** (**In a Free State**, **1971**), **Salman Rushdie** (**Midnight's Children**, **1981**), **Arundhati Roy** (**The God of Small Things**, **1997**), **Kiran Desai** (**The Inheritance of Loss**, **2006**), **Aravind Adiga** (**The White Tiger**, **2008**).
• **Pulitzer Prize**:
  • Established in **1917** by **Joseph Pulitzer**.
  • Administered by **Columbia University**.
  • Awards excellence in **newspaper journalism, literature, and musical composition** in the United States.
  • Categories include Public Service, Breaking News Reporting, Fiction, Drama, History, Poetry, Music, etc.
  • Notable Indian-origin winners: **Jhumpa Lahiri** (**Interpreter of Maladies**, **2000** - Fiction), **Siddhartha Mukherjee** (**The Emperor of All Maladies**, **2011** - General Nonfiction).

items.title: 5. Global Recognition: **Olympics** & Other Key Awards
items.content:
• **Olympic Games**:
  • Premier international multi-sport event.
  • Held every **four years** (Summer and Winter Games).
  • Medals awarded: **Gold, Silver, Bronze**.
  • Key Indian Olympic achievements: **Norman Pritchard** (first Indian-origin medalist, **1900**), **K.D. Jadhav** (first independent India medalist, **1952**), **Abhinav Bindra** (first individual Gold, **2008**).
• **Academy Awards (Oscars)**:
  • Presented by the **Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS)**.
  • Recognizes excellence in **cinematic achievements**.
  • First awarded in **1929**.
  • Key Indian winners: **Bhanu Athaiya** (Costume Design, **Gandhi**, **1983**), **Satyajit Ray** (Lifetime Achievement, **1992**), **A.R. Rahman, Gulzar, Resul Pookutty** (**Slumdog Millionaire**, **2009**).
• **Grammy Awards**:
  • Presented by the **Recording Academy**.
  • Recognizes outstanding achievements in the **music industry**.
  • First awarded in **1959**.
  • Key Indian winners: **Ravi Shankar, Zakir Hussain, A.R. Rahman**.
• **Ramon Magsaysay Award**:
  • Established in **1957**.
  • Often called **'Asia's Nobel Prize'**.
  • Recognizes greatness of spirit and transformative leadership in Asia.
  • Key Indian winners: **Vinoba Bhave** (first, **1958**), **Arvind Kejriwal, Ravish Kumar**.

items.definition: Remember **'P.E.A.C.E. L.I.T. M.E.D.'** for the six categories: **P**hysics, **E**conomics, **A**nd **C**hemistry, **E**veryone **LIT**erally **MED**itates (Physics, Economics, Chemistry, Literature, Medicine, Peace). This helps recall all fields.
Think **'R.K.V.'** for **R**ajagopalachari, **K**rishnan (Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan), **V**enkata Raman (C.V. Raman). This simple sequence helps recall the pioneering trio.
Use **'V.B.S.'** for **V**ibhushan (highest), **B**hushan (middle), **S**hri (lowest). This reflects the decreasing order of prestige among the Padma Awards.
Remember **'N.R.R.D.A.'** for **N**aipaul, **R**ushdie, **R**oy, **D**esai, **A**diga. This helps recall the sequence of Indian-origin authors who won the Booker Prize.
Think **'A.D.K.'** for **A**rjuna (**₹15 lakh**), **D**ronacharya (**₹15 lakh**), **K**hel Ratna (**₹25 lakh**). Note Arjuna and Dronacharya have the same prize, Khel Ratna is higher.
Associate **'P.S.'** for **P**eace in **S**tockholm (Incorrect! Peace is in Oslo). Correct: **'P.O.S.'** for **P**eace in **O**slo, **S**tockholm for others. This helps differentiate the two cities.
Remember **'Drona trains Arjuna'**. **Dronacharya** Award is for **coaches** (like Drona), and **Arjuna** Award is for **players** (like Arjuna). This clarifies the distinction.

items.term: Confusing Bharat Ratna and Padma Vibhushan
items.definition: Bharat Ratna is India's **highest civilian award**, while Padma Vibhushan is the **second highest**. Students often mistakenly equate them or reverse their order of precedence.
Many assume all Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm. The **Nobel Peace Prize** is uniquely awarded in **Oslo, Norway**, while the other five are in Stockholm, Sweden.

items.term: Mixing up Booker and Pulitzer Prizes
items.definition: The **Booker Prize** is for the best novel written in English and published in the **UK or Ireland**. The **Pulitzer Prize** is for excellence in **American journalism, literature, and music**. They have different geographical and category focuses.

While **Jawaharlal Nehru** received it in **1955**, the **first recipients in 1954** were **C. Rajagopalachari, Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and C.V. Raman**. Don't confuse the years or the initial list.
**Arjuna Award** is for **outstanding sportspersons** (players), while **Dronacharya Award** is for **outstanding coaches**. The distinction lies in recognizing performance vs. mentorship.
The **Olympic Games** (both Summer and Winter) are held **every four years**, not annually or biennially. The Summer and Winter Games are staggered, but each type occurs quadrennially.

The **Bharat Ratna** can be awarded **posthumously**, a provision added in **1966**. The first posthumous recipient was **Lal Bahadur Shastri**. Students sometimes assume it's only for living individuals.
The **Ramon Magsaysay Award** is often referred to as **'Asia's Nobel Prize'**, not any other regional award. This specific nickname is important.
Instituted by **Alfred Nobel** in **1901**, awarded in **Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace**, and **Economic Sciences**.
Most Nobel Prizes are awarded in **Stockholm, Sweden**, but the **Peace Prize** is awarded in **Oslo, Norway**.
India's **highest civilian award**, instituted in **1954**, maximum **three** per year, can be awarded **posthumously**.
**C. Rajagopalachari, Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman** were the first three recipients in **1954**.
Three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (second highest civilian), **Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Shri**, announced on **Republic Day**.
Recognizes **outstanding sportspersons** for performance over **four years**, instituted in **1961**, includes **₹15 lakh**.
Recognizes **outstanding coaches**, instituted in **1985**, includes **₹15 lakh**.

items.term: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award
items.definition: India's **highest sporting honour**, instituted in **1991-92**, for **spectacular performance** over **four years**, includes **₹25 lakh**.
For the **best original novel in English** published in the **UK or Ireland**, established in **1969**.
Awards excellence in **American journalism, literature, and musical composition**, established in **1917** by **Joseph Pulitzer**.
**Bhanu Athaiya** (first, **1983**), **Satyajit Ray** (Lifetime), **A.R. Rahman, Gulzar, Resul Pookutty** (**2009**).
Known as **'Asia's Nobel Prize'**, established in **1957**, first Indian recipient was **Vinoba Bhave** (**1958**).
Held **every four years** (Summer and Winter Games are staggered), awarding **Gold, Silver, Bronze** medals.
**Rabindranath Tagore** for Literature in **1913**, making him the first non-European to win.
**Pranab Mukherjee, Bhupen Hazarika, Nanaji Deshmukh** received the award in **2019**.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, focus on the **first recipients** and **most recent recipients** of major awards (Bharat Ratna, Nobel, Khel Ratna, Booker). Also, know the **year of institution** and the **field** for which each award is given. Create a timeline for quick revision.

A common trap is confusing the **cash prizes** for different sports awards (Arjuna, Dronacharya, Khel Ratna). Remember **Khel Ratna has the highest prize** (**₹25 lakh**), while Arjuna and Dronacharya have **₹15 lakh** each. Pay attention to these specific figures.

When studying international awards like the Nobel or Booker, prioritize **Indian winners** or winners of Indian origin. For the Pulitzer, focus on categories relevant to general knowledge like Fiction or Public Service, and any Indian-origin winners.

Do not confuse the **categories** of awards. For example, the Nobel Prize has six categories, but the Booker Prize is specifically for novels. Misidentifying the scope of an award is a frequent error.

For the Olympics, remember key facts like its **frequency, motto, and symbols**. Also, know the **first Indian medalists** (both pre-independence and post-independence) and any **individual gold medalists** from India.

Be careful with **posthumous awards**. While Bharat Ratna can be given posthumously, not all awards have this provision. Always verify if an award can be given after the recipient's death, as this is a common point of confusion.

keyTakeaways: **Nobel Prize** is the highest global honour, with **6 categories** and specific locations for presentation.
**Bharat Ratna** is India's top civilian award, followed by the **Padma Awards** (Vibhushan, Bhushan, Shri).
Indian sports awards include **Arjuna (players), Dronacharya (coaches)**, and **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (highest sporting honour)**.
**Booker Prize** is for English novels (UK/Ireland), while **Pulitzer Prize** is for American journalism/literature.
Key Indian Nobel Laureates: **Tagore, Raman, Mother Teresa, Amartya Sen, Kailash Satyarthi**.
First Bharat Ratna recipients: **C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman** in **1954**.
**Olympics** are held every four years, with **Gold, Silver, Bronze** medals awarded.
**Ramon Magsaysay Award** is known as 'Asia's Nobel Prize', with **Vinoba Bhave** as the first Indian recipient.
